It is an accelerated-approval filing on dystrophin, with functional improvement reported in the DELIVER registrational cohort. Rather than running up, the stock fell 28% from its pre-acceptance base to $17.02 (market cap about $3.18B). The 6/30 balance sheet held about $898M cash, plus about $355M net from the July raise, so net cash is roughly $1.1B, or about $6/share, and EV is about $2.1B. The capital structure is clean (no preferred; Hercules debt is modest), so the numerator was not inherited. It is anchored to the pre-catalyst price and a net-cash floor, not to an analyst target. Gaps: the web-search budget was exhausted, so I could not identify why the stock fell from July to November (FDA or DMD peer read-through versus sector beta), whether an AdCom is planned, or the current exon-51 competitive and regulatory context. The binary risk under current FDA posture toward DMD surrogates keeps this at WATCH until those are checked.
